text: But America's richest town has zero shops.
Why?
Meet Atherton, California, barely five square miles, about 7,000 people.
A typical home here costs $10.7 million.
That's the priciest zip code in America, nine times in 11 years.
So where does all that money go?
Nowhere, no stores, no restaurants, not even a gas station.
The town's rules allow zero business land.
Most streets don't even have sidewalks.
And a new home needs at least one full acre.
But here's the wildest part.
Atherton had a train station for over 150 years.
In 2020, it closed.
Now trains just pass through.
So why pay $10 million to live here?
Look at the map.
Stanford is next door.
Meta and Google are a short drive away.
It's Silicon Valley's quietest hiding place.
No crowds, no tourists, just trees and gates.
So dream town or just too quiet?
Either way, that's why.
